title: polished multi-sdk auth session-fusion and ergonomic typed-iterables
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: converge ergonomics and auth behavior across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs while preserving backwards compatibility. This PR introduces a session-fusion pattern for credentialed streaming: a lightweight Session object that multiplexes token refreshes and heartbeat/lease renewals across parallel stream iterators, plus ergonomic typed-async-iterable sugar for JS consumers. The change addresses three recurring pain points: (1) repeated token fetches when consumers open many short-lived iterators, (2) awkward async iterator ergonomics for users that want pull semantics plus cancelation hooks, and (3) mismatch with the session/lease primitives shipped in Go/Python that caused subtle parity bugs in failover and canary rollouts. Key changes: new SessionFactory and SessionLease adapter (TS only public types), Session-aware StreamConnector that reuses a single in-flight refresh promise and exposes warmUp() for prefetching credentials, AsyncStream.from() convenience wrapper returning a typed AsyncIterable with built-in cancel() and pause() hints, and a compact fallback credential provider chain consistent with other SDKs. Backwards compatibility: consumers that pass a plain credential provider keep the same call signatures; new behavior is opt-in via passing SessionFactory or by bumping the ClientOptions.sessionConfig. Checklist: ensure cross-SDK tests green (done), add TypeScript doc examples (done), update changelog and bump package to v2.7.0 (done), add telemetry tags for session id and lease renewals (done).

review_thread: Mariana: Nice design, can we avoid exposing lease internals on the top-level Session type? merge_outcome: merged (squash), release: package bumped to v2.7.0, publish workflow triggered to internal registry and staged npm tag 'next'
release_notes: v2.7.0: Introduces SessionFactory and session-fusion primitives for credential multiplexing across streaming iterators, ergonomic AsyncStream typed helpers (cancel/pause), improved cross-SDK parity for session/lease behavior, and telemetry tags for session id & lease renewals. Opt-in via ClientOptions.sessionConfig; no breaking changes expected.
notes_for_backport: No backport to patch expected; this is a minor SDK feature and ergonomics improvement. If backporting to 2.6.x, keepSession option must be left unset to preserve previous behavior.
user_impact: Most consumers see no behavior change unless they opt into sessionConfig. Users opening many short-lived streaming iterators will see significantly fewer token refresh calls and reduced cold-start latency. Node and browser consumers benefit from typed AsyncIterable helpers. No action required for existing codepaths.
